app.title: Voicenotes AI Notes & Meetings
app.text:
Voicenotes is the easiest way to take notes — whether you’re in a meeting, on a walk, or processing a thought out loud.
Just hit record. Voicenotes transcribes your speech instantly, summarizes what matters, and lets you ask your AI to recall anything later.

Record everything. Remember anything.

Use Voicenotes to:
Record meetings, reflections, ideas, and conversations
Get accurate transcriptions in 100+ languages
Summarize long recordings into short, clear takeaways
Ask your AI to remember details, dates, and decisions
Create content directly from your notes

It transcribed what I recorded accurately and then wrote a whole email with my ideas but in a much stronger style. It also built from my text a whole essay that answered my custom-made question. I was so impressed!

results.title: Most reliable voice dictation app with MCP
results.body: I've tried a bunch of voice dictation apps, and Voicenotes is the one I keep coming back to. It's super fast, opens right from the lock screen, and is the most reliable when it comes to recording with a spotty connection. Even with background noise, it captures everything I'm saying. I can record for a long duration and it still picks up on everything, even when I'm walking around outside (which is when I tend to record most of my longer voice notes). I really like using Voicenotes for voice journaling, and the MCP connection is a genuine game changer: it lets my AI agents access all of my voice notes, which is incredibly valuable. I highly recommend this app and really enjoy using the product.

results.title: Fundamental Reliability Problems
results.body: At the most fundamental level, a voice notes app needs to record and trust, once lost, is hard to gain back. In just two weeks of testing Voicenotes, I've lost approximately three hours of very important recordings. First incident (March 11, iPhone): I was recording a note that reached 54 minutes when I paused it. I checked back twice over the next 25 minutes and the paused recording was still there both times. When I went to resume it the third time (roughly 30mins after pausing), it had vanished completely. The company acknowledged this as an "edge case." Second incident (March 25, Mac laptop): I recorded a critical 2-hour meeting on my Mac laptop. The laptop remained on and active throughout. When the meeting ended, I pressed stop and clicked the arrow key in the Mac app (that takes you the dashboard/site). The recording disappeared and I couldn't find it anywhere. Apple Watch reliability issues: Recording on the Apple Watch never worked consistently. Recordings would stop abruptly and disappear into the ether. I didn't even report this because I gave up on that feature rather quickly. If one user can encounter two "edge cases" in about two weeks, this app is not for me. I can't trust an app that loses important content, especially when those conversations can't be recreated. Three hours of critical recordings is too much to lose. To potential users: If you're recording important content you can't afford to lose, I'd recommend testing thoroughly with non-critical recordings first, or considering more established alternatives. To the developer: The core functionality needs to be rock solid before adding features. Focus on ensuring recordings are reliably saved across all platforms. I'll be looking for other options.

results.title: Unreliable and hard to use
results.body: I really wanted to like this app, but it ended up being frustrating and unreliable. First, organizing notes is a mess. There’s no clear or effective way to categorize recordings, separate meetings, or keep projects distinct. If you record frequently, everything quickly turns into an unmanageable pile. The meeting summary and output features sound great in theory, but they don’t consistently work. I’ve had recordings sit there indefinitely without generating a summary. In one case, I had to wait until the next day and try again — and because of that delay, I ended up paying for an extra week of the subscription just to access notes that should have been available earlier. Exporting is another major pain point. There’s no bulk export option, so you have to download files one by one. On top of that, the file formats are inconsistent — some export as MP3, others as M4A — which creates extra work if you need them in a uniform format. Transcription is also unreliable. The app claims to auto-generate transcripts, but sometimes timestamps are included and sometimes they aren’t. For meeting notes and professional use, timestamps are pretty standard and often necessary, so this inconsistency makes the transcripts less useful. Overall, the app has promising ideas but poor execution. Between the organizational issues, unreliable summaries, inconsistent exports, and unpredictable transcripts, it just wasn’t worth the subscription. I canceled.
